segments.text: The radiance that rises on the face of the man who toiled, dug down into the depths, and brought up pure gold is richer in quality than the gleam that rises from the gold itself.

segments.text: The joy that blossoms in the eyes of the man who held his breath and brought up a pearl is of a higher order than the pearl's own lustre.

segments.text: The cool delight that glides through the heart of the maiden who has walked through a forest of sharp thorns and plucked the rose blooming among the thorns that scratched her is greater than the coolness of the flower itself. For months they toiled; for days they waited in expectation; they stood against the jeers and ridicule of opponents, against those who sneered, "A conference, is it?" and spoke words of ill omen; they brushed them aside—crossed the hardships that came raging at them—while the fear of how it could possibly be conducted shook them, while the doubt whether it would go well clawed at their hearts. With dignity alone as their shield, and discipline and the movement's ideals as their weapons, they took up the task of conducting the great State Conference—

segments.text: To all of them we offer our greetings as a tribute.

segments.text: How many ideas leap and play within the deep sigh breathed by those heroes! How many songs of delight pour from it! How many dances of awakening beat the drum within it!

blocks.text: How many ideas leap and play within the deep sigh breathed by those heroes! How many songs of delight pour from it! How many dances of awakening beat the drum within it!

segments.text: On a scale never before seen in the political history of the South, the procession of the victorious heroes moved: the flags of more than six hundred branch units whirled and flew like ceremonial fans; a decorated elephant swayed forward bearing the flag of the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam; champions of the cause kept watch from horseback; ranks of younger brothers came around them; comrades from the branch organisations marched district by district; garlands were showered like flowers; all along the route, people stood in row after row with folded hands, offering greetings. With hearts swelling and smiles playing on their faces, the procession stretched five miles in distance and two miles in length. That deep sigh proclaims it with pride!

That deep sigh thunders it forth!

segments.text: A four-day conference! Night and day; drama—speech—more than two hundred thousand people. Lack of facilities—lack of space—amid all these obstacles, the young bulls who never lost their ardour, the skill with which they welcomed and served all those people: that deep sigh makes all this plain! The front-line heroes sang battle songs in a manner that recalled the Chera, Chola and Pandya warriors; the two hundred thousand who listened merged completely into a flood of ethnic consciousness; that deep sigh turns that sight beyond seeing into poetry!

Such is Dravida: Dravida, the war-song of warriors whose courage swells as they vow to win it without fear even if fire rains down; Dravida, dwelling in the hearts of heroes who, even when mountains rise against them, do not lose their stance, and who sing with courage, “The flower-garden where the mango-cuckoo sings is the prison that seeks to cage us,” driving away sorrow, never slackening their speed, yearning to seize the flag of liberation. segments.text: It cannot be destroyed by the money-bombs rolled out by mansion-dwellers! It cannot be reduced to dust by the crooked words of those who say that asking, "Do you accept Dravida?" is begging for an agreement, who put a price on principle and gamble in political advertising with the cry, "Look! Look! Behold the city!" Dravida! Gold whose purity rises when cast into the fire! A diamond that shines brighter the more it is struck! A Dravidian with self-respect will not lose the gold—not even to barter it for brass!

Ministers were scheduled to speak there; Minister Parameswaran, along with ministers such as Kumarasami Raja and Perumalsami Reddiar, had gone to the place.

segments.text: But those who organised the conference, wishing to enjoy and enlarge their knowledge by listening to the bow-song *Naan Kanda Russia* ("The Russia I Saw") of Kalaivanar, the king of comedy, N. We have received a report that, the moment the ministers learnt this, they slipped away without telling anyone and without taking part in the conference. If this report is true, there can be no act more shameful than this.

segments.text: If Congress ministers take to their heels faster than the wind at the sight of this, what are we to call it? Why should these ministers run? In Russia the rains do not fall regularly. So, without depending upon the rain, they have discovered and kept ready the technique of producing the food they need! Therefore they do not fear famine. segments.text: The ministers must have known very well that, if the people understood these truths, they would also understand the causes of the Congress regime's lack of honesty, incompetence, want of integrity, selfishness and other disorders; that the people would realise that the famine prevailing in the country, the spread of bribery and corruption, and the black market becoming ubiquitous were all evils produced by the selfishness of Congressmen; and that, if the people then challenged them with questions while they spoke, they would be left struggling and choking for want of a proper answer. That must be why these ministers ran away instead of taking part in the conference.

blocks.text: The ministers must have known very well that, if the people understood these truths, they would also understand the causes of the Congress regime's lack of honesty, incompetence, want of integrity, selfishness and other disorders; that the people would realise that the famine prevailing in the country, the spread of bribery and corruption, and the black market becoming ubiquitous were all evils produced by the selfishness of Congressmen; and that, if the people then challenged them with questions while they spoke, they would be left struggling and choking for want of a proper answer. That must be why these ministers ran away instead of taking part in the conference.

segments.text: For Congress rulers, standing before a public forum, giving satisfactory answers to the people's questions, and setting their minds at rest is an impossible task. What else can they do but flee at the sight of honesty?

blocks.text: For Congress rulers, standing before a public forum, giving satisfactory answers to the people's questions, and setting their minds at rest is an impossible task. What else can they do but flee at the sight of honesty?

segments.text: Winning an election honestly, with integrity, on the strength of policy—there is no such thing in the Congress dictionary. Since victory can be secured by some intrigue or other, by importing someone from the North and dragging him around here as a spectacle, by employing many other tricks, by using official power and taking the police as an ally, the Congress rulers have hardened their hearts into believing that there is no need to stand before a public forum at all; that they can gather black-marketeers, permit-holders, licence-holders and contractors somewhere, display those gatherings as public forums, and deceive those who speak of democracy. What else can such rulers do but run from the truth!

Born upon this holy land, blessed by Mother Bharat, endowed by the grace of the inner soul with the power to achieve whatever they think of—(the power to achieve what they think of means ordering a trade in children and piling up mountains of corpses)—the great and mighty holy men seated upon ministerial thrones apparently judged that even looking upon the face of the sinner who had been to Russia would be a pollution, and so sprang away with their heels striking the backs of their heads.

segments.text: The lords who wield the sceptre trembled at the clown's voice. Srivilliputhur is the constituency in which Kamarasar is contesting! In that place, the oppressed wished to hold a conference. Those who screamed themselves hoarse claiming to labour for the oppressed ran away after humiliating the heroes of the durbar. The man who had been to Russia—if he were to tell the oppressed of the joys that flourish in Russia...... if all those oppressed people were then to shout aloud at our famine ministers, "O rulers who came to govern! Listen, sir, to Russia's merriment!"—what would they do? It was out of that fear that they ran.

segments.text: After we announced at the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam State Conference our decision on whom to support in the election, the Communist paper *Janasakthi* wrote that the resolution was deeply disappointing and would help Kamarajars and Samiyappas win.

blocks.text: After we announced at the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam State Conference our decision on whom to support in the election, the Communist paper *Janasakthi* wrote that the resolution was deeply disappointing and would help Kamarajars and Samiyappas win.

segments.text: Why the Communists—who in fact shake hands with those officially working for Samiyappa's victory—should heap this baseless charge upon us, we do not understand!

blocks.text: Why the Communists—who in fact shake hands with those officially working for Samiyappa's victory—should heap this baseless charge upon us, we do not understand!

segments.text: If we refuse to live by selling our shame and joining those who called our movement "cast-offs," to say that we are therefore helping our enemies to win is thoroughly false propaganda.

blocks.text: If we refuse to live by selling our shame and joining those who called our movement "cast-offs," to say that we are therefore helping our enemies to win is thoroughly false propaganda.

segments.text: At the very moment we extended the hand of friendship, they brushed it aside, insulted our fundamental issue, and called us only with the words, "Come just for the election." And now they say, "Not to drink the honey of the election"—

blocks.text: At the very moment we extended the hand of friendship, they brushed it aside, insulted our fundamental issue, and called us only with the words, "Come just for the election." And now they say, "Not to drink the honey of the election"—

segments.text: —and point out that they did not invite us in order to form a Communist government. These remain riddles we cannot understand.

blocks.text: —and point out that they did not invite us in order to form a Communist government. These remain riddles we cannot understand.

segments.text: Samiyappa took pains in Thanjavur district to work for the destruction of the Communists. After making platforms thunder with speeches that it would be a great cruelty to let him win, after painting word-pictures to that effect in their papers, what name are we to give to the act of standing in fellowship with those who support him? We do not know.

We do not know.

segments.text: A feast in the capitalist's house on one side; a sermon on wiping away the worker's suffering on the other! What a contradiction to the courage—and the policy—of the Communists! Was it for such a grotesque United Front that we invited them?

blocks.text: A feast in the capitalist's house on one side; a sermon on wiping away the worker's suffering on the other! What a contradiction to the courage—and the policy—of the Communists! Was it for such a grotesque United Front that we invited them?

segments.text: If we had been working together, would we oppose K. D. Rasu in Erode? Would we try to defeat Mohan Kumar Mangalam in Salem?

blocks.text: If we had been working together, would we oppose K. D. Rasu in Erode? Would we try to defeat Mohan Kumar Mangalam in Salem?

segments.text: At a meeting in Kanchipuram, comrade Jeevanandam said: "Periyar asked us to give way to Samiyappa—

blocks.text: At a meeting in Kanchipuram, comrade Jeevanandam said: "Periyar asked us to give way to Samiyappa—

segments.text: —give way to that murderous sinner?"

blocks.text: —give way to that murderous sinner?"

segments.text: According to Jeevanandam's own dictionary, the Communist mind can cultivate relations with the mentality that asked them to yield to a murderous sinner! But we invited them to an orderly—firm—unmutilated United Front, and the Communists could not agree to it! Not only did they refuse agreement; they began to reject the very question that is life itself to us.

But we invited them to an orderly—firm—unmutilated United Front, and the Communists could not agree to it! Not only did they refuse agreement; they began to reject the very question that is life itself to us.

segments.text: They can maintain relations with those who say that *Janasakthi* is not a Communist paper! But they are afraid even to approach us—who respect *Janasakthi*, try to answer its doubts, and desire friendship!

blocks.text: They can maintain relations with those who say that *Janasakthi* is not a Communist paper! But they are afraid even to approach us—who respect *Janasakthi*, try to answer its doubts, and desire friendship!

segments.text: Policy has reached such a state that they can keep friendship with those who refused to recognise the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam as an organisation and failed to understand democracy, yet they tremble at friendship with a great force functioning democratically!

blocks.text: Policy has reached such a state that they can keep friendship with those who refused to recognise the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam as an organisation and failed to understand democracy, yet they tremble at friendship with a great force functioning democratically!

segments.text: The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam did not say that it could not support the Communists. The Communists themselves created the circumstances that made support impossible! It was not merely that they did not agree with our question—they declared that our question itself was wrong!

blocks.text: The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam did not say that it could not support the Communists. The Communists themselves created the circumstances that made support impossible! It was not merely that they did not agree with our question—they declared that our question itself was wrong!

segments.text: Those who said from public platforms that "Dravida Nadu is just"—why did they refuse to sign the agreement document? That is the question to be thought about!

blocks.text: Those who said from public platforms that "Dravida Nadu is just"—why did they refuse to sign the agreement document? That is the question to be thought about!

segments.text: When one predicts that even those who signed the document will change, how are we to believe that those who merely spoke from platforms without signing it will remain unchanged?

blocks.text: When one predicts that even those who signed the document will change, how are we to believe that those who merely spoke from platforms without signing it will remain unchanged?

segments.text: Are we people who, on one side, make a show of supporting the Communists and, on the other, use the Communists to frighten capitalists and conduct an election trade?

blocks.text: Are we people who, on one side, make a show of supporting the Communists and, on the other, use the Communists to frighten capitalists and conduct an election trade?

segments.text: We wish to say something emphatically to the Communists. We remind them once of a golden saying from *Viduthalai* (20-12-51).

blocks.text: We wish to say something emphatically to the Communists. We remind them once of a golden saying from *Viduthalai* (20-12-51).

segments.text: Let *Viduthalai*'s golden saying be a lesson to them! "The husband who treats the wife who lives with him in true affection with contempt, and then, bewitched by the sidelong glance and coquettish speech of a dancing prostitute, runs after her, is bound one day to come to his senses."

segments.text: We know very well that the Communists do not regard the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam as a weak party. The Communists know well that the DMK is not a party in which the leader—newspaper editor—orator—committee—secretary, statement-issuer, adviser and treasurer are all one man conducting it in many different incarnations!

segments.text: Nor do the Communists show us affection merely because we are "ten or fifteen youngsters! Poor fellows; good boys." They know our strength from the fact that those ten or fifteen youngsters conducted a conference that made even enemies marvel—and made old men burn with envy.

segments.text: On that very day, when two or three meetings around Madras had been held with tremendous publicity—

segments.text: —they also know that we had settled in the hearts of the people deeply enough to conduct a great conference attended by two hundred thousand.

segments.text: The Communists respect our strength.

blocks.text: The Communists respect our strength.

segments.text: Not only the Communists; even Congressmen respect our strength. That is why, to some extent, they have come forward to publish our news instead of completely blacking us out!

segments.text: To say that we are Congress kanganis because Congress papers publish our news is jealousy distilled to its purest form! Communist papers too published news of the conference. Does that make us Communist kanganis? Socialist papers too carried it on a large scale. Does that make us Socialist kanganis? *Dina Thanthi* too carried it; does that make us Praja Party kanganis?

segments.text: Can one therefore say that Periyar was connected with Madhava Menon? There was hardly a platform on which Periyar did not speak in support of Omandurar! Does that make Periyar a Congress kangani? Why, Congress papers even give space to Communist programmes and speeches. Does that make the Communists Congress kanganis?

Sharma, who has built a Kali temple, and when no one crowns that act with the title "Aryan kangani," I cannot understand what wondrous judgement of which "God of Justice" it is to call people who are without fault and who have not betrayed their principles kanganis!

segments.text: Comrades who say that our course is one that seeks a path to Congress victory must think carefully.

segments.text: For many years we have proclaimed the ideal of "Dravida Nadu"!

blocks.text: For many years we have proclaimed the ideal of "Dravida Nadu"!

segments.text: From Salem onward we have also proclaimed that we ourselves would not stand in the election! By right—by the strength we possess—we ought to have contested the election ourselves. Since that situation did not arise, we decided to support those who oppose the Congress.

segments.text: We wanted the person so supported to be one who would argue for our fundamental question in the Assembly. We ourselves are not in the Assembly! There is nothing wrong—and nothing meaningless—in wanting at least our voice to be heard there!

segments.text: ஜி. பி. சோமசுந்தரம் வயது சுமார் அறுபது! கே. கே. நீலமேகம் வயது சுமார் ஐம்பது! பொள்ளாச்சி நடராசு வயது சுமார் அறுபது! பெத்தாம் பாளையம் பழனிச்சாமி வயது ஏறக்குறைய நாற்பது! நெடுஞ்செழியன் சுமார் வயது முப்பது! சேலம் சித்தையன் வயது சுமார் நாற்பது! இ. வி. கே. சம்பத் வயது சுமார் இருபத்தேழு. சி. பி. சிற்றரசு வயது சுமார் நாற்பது! என். வி. நடராசன் வயது சுமார் நாற்பது! பார்த்தசாரதி வயது நிச்சயமாக நாற்பத்திரண்டு! அப்பாதுரையார் வயது சுமார் ஐம்பது! மணிமொழியார் வயது அநேகமாக ஐம்பத்திநாலு! எஸ். வி. லிங்கம் கிழவரே! மூதாட்டி ராமாமிர்தத்தம்மாள் முப்பது வயது! segments.text: Yet, for some reason I do not know, poor G. P. Somasundaram and people like Pollachi Natarasu are called youngsters. Under government law, those above eighteen are adults who are no longer "minors"! Surely no one would call them youngsters without even knowing that. "Youngsters" means people who possess young hearts even in old age!

An heir! A clod of earth!

segments.text: The man contesting against him is comrade P. Balasubramaniam, editor of the *Sunday Observer*, supported by the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam. segments.text: Koyanga is trying to come across our struggle for a separate Dravidian state and plant his flag in its path! A northern magnate; a representative of the deceivers who set up moneylending shops and turned fertile Tamil land into a parched land; an emissary of the class that, after the days when it lay at the Tamils' feet, now learns at the Tamils' feet only to bring Tamils low—he has entered the Tindivanam region and raised the battle cry against Tirukkural Munisami, at a time when the strong shoulders of Dravidian warriors have not yet worn thin in Dravida!

segments.text: We see little jackals wielding the sceptre in the lion's cave. At a time when many valiant Dravidians are labouring to put an end to that cowardice, Koyanga has made his entrance.

segments.text: If one of the commanders of Dravida's permanent enemies, who wear Dravida down through *Dinamani*, now seeks to beat the drum of victory and sing a heroic ode in Tindivanam, what greater hour of trial need come to the warriors?

segments.text: In ancient days a hero placed stones on the heads of the northern Kanaka-Visayars who had insulted the Dravidians and dragged them back. Now that lineage of Kanaka-Visayars comes toward Dravida to defeat the lineage of the Cheras.

segments.text: The Tindivanam constituency must not forget that every vote cast for Koyanga is an explosive blast delivered against Dravidian life!

segments.text: The mill-kings are in the North! Political leadership is in the North! The sceptre of government is in the North! Holding all these grips, the North that gives no honour to national Chidambaram who pulled the oil-press, the North that does not even think of Tiruppur Kumaran, the North that sings no praise of Thillaiyadi Valliammai, the North that exploits the South, the North that lives by trampling Dravida—this North has decided to field a candidate in Dravida itself and weigh the measure of Dravida's gullibility!

segments.text: On another day, those who came to exploit Dravida came driving cattle through the passes of the Himalayas!

segments.text: Even now, those who come to us driving cattle are labouring to turn Dravida into a deer caught in the northerner's net.

blocks.text: Even now, those who come to us driving cattle are labouring to turn Dravida into a deer caught in the northerner's net.

segments.text: They are slaves of the North. The cattle they drive are trying to make us too slaves of the North for many more years.

segments.text: It is not merely an attempt to stamp northern civilisation, northern language and northern culture upon Dravida; through these cattle-drivers, an intense effort is under way to turn Dravida into the North's permanent lackey.

segments.text: Nor did freedom come solely through their ability and sacrifice.

segments.text: We attained freedom; we too rejoiced. Even then, we did not fail to point out that the crisis that had overtaken the white man, the situation he faced after the World War—the condition in which he could no longer hold India together—were also important reasons for liberation.

segments.text: “We have explained many times before the people that Dravida is a separate country. Its questions and institutions cannot be looked at only through one eye, from one angle, using the questions and institutions of another country.”

blocks.text: “We have explained many times before the people that Dravida is a separate country. Its questions and institutions cannot be looked at only through one eye, from one angle, using the questions and institutions of another country.”

segments.text: But some, in the manner of
“the hare I caught has only three legs,”

merely prophesied that it was impossible, impracticable, narrow-minded; merely tried to hide our heart's song by dragging in another country as an example; became slaves to doctrines and enemies of practice; and remained people who did not understand the inner meaning of our question.

segments.text: Those who showed themselves openly as enemies opposed our question directly! Those who did not show themselves did so indirectly. It was to bring all these forms of opposition to an end that we decided to support in the election those who accept the Dravida Nadu question.

segments.text: திருப்பத்தூரிலே திராவிட முன்னேற்றக் கழக ஆதரவு பெற்றவரும் ஒப்பந்த ஏட்டில் கையெழுத்திட்டவருமான தோழர் ராகவன் அவர்கள் வெற்றி பெற்றுவிட்டார் என்ற செய்தியும், மதுரையிலே கம்யூனிஸ்ட் தோழர் ராமமூர்த்தி அவர்கள் வெற்றி பெற்று விட்டார் என்ற செய்தியும், உதயகிரி தொகுதியில் நிதி மந்திரி கோபாலர் தோல்வியுற்றார் என்ற செய்தியும், அமலாபுரம் தொகுதியில் காளா வெங்கட்டராவ் தோல்வியுற்றார் என்ற செய்தியும், திராவிடத்தில் தேன் பாய்ச்சும் செய்திகளாக மதிக்கப்படுகின்றன.

segments.text: ஆல்பர்ட் ஜேசுதாசன் திராவிட நாட்டுப் பிரச்சினையைச் சட்டசபையில் முழக்குவேன் என்றார். ஜீவா அது இயலாது என்றார். நாம் ஆல்பர்டை ஆதரிக்கிறோம். இம்மாதிரியான சூழ்நிலை இல்லாத இடத்தில் கம்யூனிஸ்டுகளை எதிர்க்காதது மட்டுமல்ல, கழக பூர்வமாய் ஆதரிக்காவிட்டாலுங்கூட நம்முடைய ஓட்டுக்களை கம்யூனிஸ்டுகளுக்கே வழங்குவோம் என்ற உணர்ச்சிதான் பரவியிருக்கிறது. கம்யூனிஸ்டுகளை ஆதரிக்கிறோம் என்று சொல்லிவிட்டு மோகனை, கே. டி. ராஜூவை, இன்னும் பல கம்யூனிஸ்டு நண்பர்களை எதிர்த்திடும் விபரீதப்போக்கு கொண்டவர்கள் அல்ல நாம்.

segments.text: In Tiruppattur, Comrade Raghavan, who received the support of the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam and signed the agreement document, has won; in Madurai, Communist Comrade Ramamurthi has won; in the Udayagiri constituency Finance Minister Gopalar has been defeated; in the Amalapuram constituency Kala Venkata Rao has been defeated—these are regarded as tidings that pour honey into Dravida.

segments.text:
The Perumal cattle-handler got angry. Unable to say anything in his rage, he sounded the instrument: boom, boom, boom.
When he stopped, the cattle began nodding their heads.
That nodding made it seem as though they were saying: want oilcake, want cottonseed!
